samples.text:
The pie charts shows how a city council spent its budget on six different areas in 2010 and in 2025.

In 2010, education received the most money with 34% of the budget. Social care was second with 22% and transport was 15%. Housing and administration was both 10%, and parks and culture got the least, only 9%.

In 2025, the situation changed. Social care became the biggest part of budget, it increased to 35%. Education decreased to 30% and so it was the second. Transport also went down to 12%. Parks and culture fell to 5% and administration fell to 7%. So the council gave less money for these areas than in 2010. Housing was the only other area which increase, but only a little to 11%.

Overall, the council spent more on social care in 2025 than in 2010, and less on almost all other areas. The biggest change was the social care, which went up by 13%, and the parks and culture was nearly halved.
samples.why: Accurate figures for all categories · overview placed last and repeats earlier points · mechanical linking · limited range of vocabulary · several agreement, article and verb form errors that do not affect clarity.

samples.text:
The pie charts illustrate how a city council divided its budget between six areas of spending in 2010 and 2025.

Overall, the most significant change was the large increase in the share of the budget spent on social care, which replaced education as the largest category. Most other areas received a smaller proportion of funding in 2025 than in 2010.

In 2010, education was allocated just over a third of the budget (34%), while social care accounted for 22%. Transport received 15%, and housing and administration were each given 10%. Parks and culture had the smallest share, at 9%.

By 2025, social care had risen by 13 percentage points to 35%, making it the council's main area of expenditure. Education, by contrast, dropped slightly to 30%. The shares for transport and administration also fell, to 12% and 7% respectively, and spending on parks and culture was almost halved, falling to only 5%. Housing was the only other category to see an increase, although this was very small, from 10% to 11%.
samples.why: Clear overview identifying the main change · key features highlighted with accurate figures and correct derived values · logical paragraphing · good range of cohesive devices · appropriate vocabulary with few errors.

samples.text:
The charts compare the allocation of a city council's budget across six service areas in 2010 and 2025.

The standout development over the fifteen-year period was the rapid growth of social care, which overtook education to become the largest item of expenditure. This expansion was accompanied by a shrinking share for most other services, nearly all of which received a smaller proportion of the budget by 2025.

In 2010, education absorbed 34% of council spending, comfortably ahead of social care at 22%. Transport accounted for 15%, while housing and administration each took 10%, and parks and culture received the smallest share, at 9%.

By 2025, the share devoted to social care had climbed to 35%, an increase of 13 percentage points, whereas education had slipped to 30%. Transport and administration were both cut back, to 12% and 7% respectively, but the sharpest proportional reduction was in parks and culture, whose share almost halved to just 5%. Housing was the only other area to gain funding, and even then only marginally, rising by a single point to 11%. Taken together, education and social care accounted for almost two-thirds of the budget in 2025, compared with 56% in 2010.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected with a clear, well-placed overview · accurate, purposeful use of derived figures · smooth, well-managed cohesion · precise and natural vocabulary · wide range of structures, error-free.
